schema_note: Structure and taxonomy codes defined in EVAL_PLAN.md Tier 1 ('Scenario coverage taxonomy'). Owner-authored starter set: 22 cases on 2026-06-13, expanded to 74 on 2026-09-05 by filling the domain x act x input_mode matrix, then to 82 on 2026-09-06 with 8 implicit-cue twins (pair_of) and check_it draft_quality tags (docs/exec-plans/2026-09-06-eval-case-criteria-revision.md). Real user text is prohibited here. 'id' is stable and never renumbered. check_it draft_quality labels were reviewed by a native US English speaker on 2026-09-06; 024 moved good -> flawed (register: a real American patient would not phrase it this elaborately, not sentence length), 043/074 marked as pragmatic flaws in natural English; 064 kept good per the reviewer, with a firmer close offered only as an extra option.

cases.input_text: 병원 접수할 때 한국어 통역이 필요하다고 말하고 싶어. 미안해하는 느낌 없이 당연한 권리처럼 분명하게.
expected_behaviors: Variant 1 states the need for a Korean interpreter as a plain, entitled request, not an apology (tone_match)
At least one variant is short enough to say at a busy front desk without rehearsal (naturalness)
Cultural tip notes that US clinics receiving federal funds are expected to provide interpreters and that asking is routine (cultural_appropriateness)
No variant frames the user's English as a personal deficiency to apologize for (accuracy)
expected_failure_modes: Variant 1 opens with 'Sorry, my English is not good' and buries the request
Uses 'translator' interchangeably with 'interpreter' without the natural clinic wording
Cultural tip is generic ('be polite to staff') instead of naming that interpreter access is standard
All three variants are near-identical rewordings of 'I need an interpreter'

cases.input_text: 의사가 검사 결과 설명할 때 "Could you go over that again a bit slower? I want to make sure I've got it."라고 했는데 괜찮았어?
expected_behaviors: Variant 1 uses plainer, more direct phrasing that a real American patient would actually say in the exam room, not a more elaborate or formal request; a native reviewer judged the draft as something a real American would not phrase that way in this moment (naturalness)
No variant or tip implies the draft was rude or unclear; the named problem is register (too elaborate/formal for the moment), not politeness or clarity (accuracy)
Other variants offer genuinely different strategies (e.g., asking the doctor to write it down, asking for the key point), not rewordings (naturalness)
Cultural tip confirms this is a normal patient request that doctors expect (cultural_appropriateness)
expected_failure_modes: Variant 1 keeps or adds formal/elaborate phrasing a real patient would not use in the moment
Output implies the user was rude or unclear when they were not
Adds an unnecessary apology such as 'I'm sorry to bother you' to the repaired version

cases.input_text: 간호사가 퇴원 후 약 먹는 법 설명하는데 잘 못 알아듣고 그냥 "Okay, okay, yes"만 했어. 다음엔 어떻게 말해야 했을까
expected_behaviors: expressions[0].cultural_tip names why the original 'Okay, okay, yes' was a problem: it signaled understanding the user did not have (accuracy)
Variant 1 honestly says the user did not follow and asks for the instructions again, matching the frank tone (tone_match)
At least one variant asks for written instructions or a teach-back, which is standard US discharge practice (cultural_appropriateness)
Phrasing is everyday patient English, not clinical vocabulary (naturalness)
expected_failure_modes: Treats 'Okay, okay, yes' as acceptable and simply offers alternatives without flagging the risk
Repaired variant apologizes repeatedly instead of stating plainly that the user did not understand
Uses abstract wording like 'clarify the regimen' that a patient would not say
Cultural tip fails to mention that nurses expect patients to ask and it is not embarrassing

cases.input_text: 병원 청구서에 받은 적 없는 검사 항목이 있어서 청구 부서에 전화로 따지려고 해. 단호하게.
expected_behaviors: Variant 1 clearly disputes the specific charge and asks for it to be removed or reviewed, not merely 'asks about' it (tone_match)
At least one variant asks for an itemized bill or a reference number, reflecting how US billing disputes actually proceed (cultural_appropriateness)
Wording is firm without accusing the billing agent personally of fraud (naturalness)
Variants differ in escalation level, e.g., first call vs. after being brushed off (accuracy)
expected_failure_modes: Softens the firm intent into 'I was just wondering if maybe there is a mistake'
Sounds hostile or threatens legal action in variant 1 when a firm dispute was asked for
Literal translation of '따지다' producing something like 'I want to argue about my bill'
Cultural tip does not mention itemized bills, EOBs, or documenting the call

cases.input_text: 약국에서 30분 기다렸는데 약이 안 나와. "Excuse me, my medicine is not ready? I am waiting 30 minutes." 이렇게 말하려는데 자연스럽게 고쳐줘
expected_behaviors: Variant 1 repairs the draft into natural pharmacy-counter English that mentions the wait and asks for a status or estimate (naturalness)
Keeps the user's core content (prescription, 30 minutes, not ready) rather than replacing it with a different situation (accuracy)
Tone stays polite but does not retreat into a pure apology; it still expects an answer (tone_match)
Pronunciation tip targets a real hard sound in the repaired sentence, such as 'prescription' clusters (naturalness)
expected_failure_modes: Keeps the tense error 'I am waiting 30 minutes' or the rising-question fragment
Over-corrects into a complaint that sounds angry at the pharmacy tech
Drops the 30-minute detail, losing the reason the request is reasonable
Uses 'medicine' where 'prescription' is the natural counter word without adjusting

cases.input_text: 병원에 전화해서 "Hi, I'd like to book a follow-up with Dr. Patel. What's the earliest opening you have?"라고 했어. 이상한 데 없었어?
expected_behaviors: Variant 1 (expressions[0].english) keeps the user's draft essentially as-is, changing at most a few words (accuracy)
No variant's english or cultural_tip implies the draft was rude, unclear, or too direct; expressions[0].cultural_tip says it was appropriate for this situation (accuracy)
Alternative variants add genuinely different options, e.g., offering availability windows or asking about a cancellation list (naturalness)
Cultural tip is specific to scheduler calls, such as being ready with insurance and date of birth (cultural_appropriateness)
expected_failure_modes: Rewrites the fine sentence into a longer, stiffer version
Claims 'What's the earliest opening' is too demanding when it is standard phrasing
Cultural tip is generic ('be polite on the phone')

cases.input_text: my 4-year-old daughter has had a fever of 102 since last night and tylenol isn't helping. calling the nurse line, what do I say
expected_behaviors: Handles English-only input gracefully and still returns valid JSON with exactly 3 expressions (accuracy)
Variants state the key facts a triage nurse needs: age (4), temperature (102), duration (since last night), what was tried (Tylenol) (accuracy)
Phrasing is concise phone English a worried parent would actually say, not a medical report (naturalness)
tone_label, pronunciation_tip, and cultural_tip are still in Korean per schema even though input was English (accuracy)
Tone range is appropriate for a worried but composed parent when tone_intent is null (tone_match)
expected_failure_modes: Refuses or asks for Korean input instead of answering
Switches Korean-required fields (tone_label, tips) to English because the input was English
Omits the temperature or duration, which the nurse line will ask first
Gives medical advice instead of expressions to say

cases.input_text: 은행 콜센터에 30분 기다려 연결됐는데 본인 확인 질문을 못 알아들었어. 당황하지 않고 천천히 다시 말해달라고 하고 싶어
expected_behaviors: Variant 1 calmly asks the agent to repeat or rephrase the verification question, without self-blame (tone_match)
At least one variant asks the agent to spell or slow down a specific item, which is how phone repair actually works (naturalness)
Cultural tip notes that call-center agents expect repeat requests and that the user should not answer a question they did not understand (cultural_appropriateness)
Pronunciation tip targets phone-clarity sounds in the chosen expression (naturalness)
expected_failure_modes: Opens with 'Sorry, my English is bad' and sounds flustered rather than calm
Uses vague 'I don't understand' with no specific repair request
Suggests guessing an answer to the security question
Cultural tip is generic

cases.input_text: 인터넷 회사에 벌써 두 번 전화했는데 아직도 안 고쳐줘. 이번엔 상급자 바꿔달라고 단호하게 말할 거야
expected_behaviors: Variant 1 references the prior two calls and asks to be transferred to a supervisor in firm, non-negotiable wording (tone_match)
At least one variant asks for a ticket or case number, reflecting real escalation practice (cultural_appropriateness)
Firmness is directed at the outcome, not at insulting the agent (naturalness)
Variants span from firm-but-cooperative to firmest, not from soft to firm (tone_match)
expected_failure_modes: Variant 1 hedges with 'if possible' or 'would it be okay' and loses the firm intent
Sounds abusive toward the agent
Omits the history of two prior calls, which is the leverage for escalation
Literal rendering like 'change to your superior person'

cases.input_text: 통신사에 전화해서 "I was charged twice this month. Can you look into it and reverse the second charge?"라고 했는데 너무 세게 말한 건 아니지?
expected_behaviors: Variant 1 (expressions[0].english) keeps the user's draft essentially as-is, changing at most a few words (accuracy)
Light warming of the slightly stiff wording (e.g., 'It looks like I was charged twice this month') counts as polish, not a rewrite, as long as the meaning and firmness stay (naturalness)
No variant softens the draft into a hedged version; expressions[0].cultural_tip says the draft was appropriately firm (tone_match)
Alternatives offer different strategies, such as asking for the charge dates or a confirmation email (naturalness)
Cultural tip notes that stating the problem and desired fix directly is the expected register with customer service (cultural_appropriateness)
expected_failure_modes: Agrees with the user's worry and rewrites the sentence more apologetically
Adds 'I'm sorry to bother you' to the repaired variant
Claims 'reverse the charge' is unnatural when it is standard

cases.input_text: 상담원이 너무 빨리 말해서 "Sorry, sorry, my English is not good"을 세 번이나 했어. 이러지 않고 다시 말해달라고 하려면?
expected_behaviors: expressions[0].cultural_tip names why repeating 'Sorry, my English is not good' was a problem: it shifted focus away from the actual repair need (accuracy)
Variant 1 asks the agent to slow down or repeat with no apology at all, satisfying the negative-form tone (tone_match)
At least one variant puts the request on the agent's pace ('you're going a bit fast for me') rather than on the user's ability (naturalness)
Cultural tip states that agents are trained to slow down on request and that apologizing is unnecessary (cultural_appropriateness)
expected_failure_modes: Repaired variant still contains 'sorry' or 'my English is not good'
Treats the user's original as fine
Over-corrects into a rude 'Speak slower'
Cultural tip is generic

cases.input_text: 전기회사에 이메일 보내려고 해. "I am writing to complain my bill is very high this month. Please check and answer me quickly." 자연스럽게 고쳐줘
expected_behaviors: Variant 1 is a natural written-register sentence or short email body that questions the bill and asks for a review, keeping both polite and firm elements (tone_match)
Repair adds what a utility company needs to act: account reference, the month, a request for a usage breakdown or meter check; placeholders such as [account number] are acceptable (accuracy)
Fixes 'complain my bill' and 'answer me quickly' into idiomatic written English (naturalness)
Cultural tip mentions email conventions such as a subject line or including the account number (cultural_appropriateness)
expected_failure_modes: Produces spoken-style variants instead of written register
Keeps 'complain my bill' or 'answer me quickly' unchanged
Drops the firm element and becomes a meek inquiry
Cultural tip talks about phone calls instead of email

cases.input_text: 집주인한테 히터 고쳐달라고 세 번 말했는데 계속 무시해. 이번엔 서면으로 보내고 시에 신고할 수도 있다고 단호하게 말하고 싶어
expected_behaviors: Variant 1 references the three prior requests, states this is now in writing, and names the next step (city or code enforcement) without bluffing (tone_match)
Phrasing fits a tenant-to-landlord relationship: firm and documented, not threatening or emotional (naturalness)
Cultural tip reflects the talk-then-write-then-report sequence and the value of dated written records (cultural_appropriateness)
At least one variant proposes a repair deadline; a placeholder such as [date] or 'by the end of this week' is acceptable since the input gives none (accuracy)
expected_failure_modes: Softens to 'I would really appreciate it if you could...' losing the escalation
Sounds like a legal threat or insult rather than a firm notice
Omits the prior-request history
Cultural tip is generic instead of naming written notice or the housing authority

cases.input_text: 집주인이 렌트를 200달러 올리겠대. 오래 살았고 문제 없었으니 인상폭을 줄여달라고 정중하지만 물러서지 않게 협상하고 싶어
expected_behaviors: Variant 1 makes a concrete counter (smaller increase or phased increase) backed by tenure and reliability, keeping both politeness and firmness (tone_match)
Leverage points (on-time payment, low turnover cost for the landlord) are stated as reasons, the way US tenants actually negotiate (accuracy)
Variants differ in strategy: counteroffer, ask for something in return, request time to consider (naturalness)
Cultural tip notes that negotiating a rent increase is normal and does not offend a landlord (cultural_appropriateness)
expected_failure_modes: Pleads or emphasizes hardship instead of negotiating from value
Retreats into 'if that's okay with you' so no counteroffer is actually made
Sounds confrontational for a relationship the user wants to keep
Cultural tip is generic

cases.input_text: 이사 30일 전 통지문 초안이야. "Dear landlord, I will move out from the apartment on October 31. Please give back my deposit." 격식 있게 고쳐줘

Preserves the October 31 date and 30-day-notice function (accuracy)
Cultural tip mentions that written notice is typically required by the lease and that the notice should be dated (cultural_appropriateness)
expected_failure_modes: Returns spoken-register variants instead of written notice language
Keeps 'give back my deposit' or 'Dear landlord' unchanged
Omits the move-out date
Cultural tip is generic instead of naming lease notice requirements

cases.input_text: 보증금에서 400달러 뗀다길래 "I'd like an itemized list of the deductions before I agree to anything."이라고 했어. 괜찮았어?
expected_behaviors: Variant 1 (expressions[0].english) keeps the user's draft essentially as-is, changing at most a few words (accuracy)
